meta.purpose: A review queue, not a to-do list. Every entry states the suggested change, the evidence behind it, the effort, and what would have to be true before it is safe to ship. Nothing here is implemented on the reader-facing side until it is marked shipped.
meta.how_to_use: Read the shortlist at the top. Each item has an id. If you want one implemented, note the id on the Suggestions page in the site and it becomes a task with a named scope.

scoring.impact: 1 = cosmetic. 5 = changes whether a reader buys or whether the shop can earn at all.
scoring.effort: 1 = under an hour and needs nothing we do not have. 5 = weeks, or needs an account, a test unit or a paid service.
scoring.confidence: High only where a source or a measurement supports the effect. 'Hypothesis' means nobody has measured it yet, including us.

shortlist.why: Unblocks the only measurement that matters: whether a click is ever attributed.
The one number a buyer wants and we are not allowed to publish yet; this is how it becomes publishable.
Seventeen pages compete for one host; consolidating is the highest-leverage SEO change available.
Turns 'we have no data' into a first-party number, without cookies.
Testimonials are the difference between a listing and a shop; this is the compliant route to getting them.

suggestions.title: Lead every product page with a plain-English verdict, then the claims
suggestions.why: A buyer decides in the first screen. A page that opens with a register of identifiers gives them nothing to decide with. Each product page now opens with a quick take written from the listing's own words, then a labelled claims table.
suggestions.confidence: Hypothesis with strong face validity; no traffic data yet.
suggestions.evidence_needed: None to ship. Time-on-page and outbound clicks would confirm it.
suggestions.shipped_note: Live: the five product pages in shop/products/.

suggestions.title: Put the disclosure in a strip under the masthead on every page, and again in the footer
suggestions.why: The FTC's test is whether a reader can weigh the recommendation at the moment they read it. A footer-only disclosure fails that on a long page. Amazon's Agreement section 5 requires the statement to be clear and prominent.
suggestions.confidence: High — a stated obligation, not a hypothesis.
suggestions.evidence_needed: None. Sources are quoted on the Sources page.
suggestions.shipped_note: Generated by one template and now enforced by tools/shop_check.py, which fails the build if the strip is missing or appears after the first outbound product link.

suggestions.title: Publish no price, rating, review count or availability figure anywhere
suggestions.why: Program Policies 2(b) permits price and availability display only where Amazon serves the link carrying the data, or where it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. No feed is connected. A stale price is also a misrepresentation risk under the same section.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.shipped_note: Every product page states what is excluded and why, in a block directly under the buy button, so the absence reads as a decision rather than a gap.

suggestions.title: Keep the submitted code and the observed ASIN in separate fields, and say so in public
suggestions.why: The submitted code is a 9-character short-link slug; the ASIN is the 10-character code after /dp/. Merging them destroys the audit trail that would catch a wrong-product redirect.
suggestions.confidence: High — Amazon's own definition of an ASIN is quoted on the page.
suggestions.shipped_note: Product pages show the observed ASIN; a table of record shows the submitted code beside it, labelled, with the observation date.

suggestions.title: Link to direct tagged amazon.com/dp/ URLs, not through the supplied short links
suggestions.why: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates tag as a URL parameter on each link, and the Agreement prohibits anything that obscures the Amazon destination. Direct /dp/ URLs with ?tag= satisfy both conditions visibly. This does not assert that the supplied links are invalid — their status remains unresolved on the Flagged page.
suggestions.confidence: High on the policy text; medium on the commercial effect, because attribution still has to be confirmed in the account.
suggestions.evidence_needed: One-link test in the Associates dashboard (see SUG-21).
suggestions.shipped_note: Every buy button uses a direct /dp/ URL carrying ?tag=shopnow047c-20 and rel="sponsored nofollow noopener". Each page also lists the supplied short link for transparency.

suggestions.title: Build a publication front page instead of a dashboard
suggestions.why: A dashboard tells the reader about the seller's process. A front page tells the reader what the shop sells and why it is worth two minutes. Naming, typography, photography and section order now read as a shop.
suggestions.confidence: Hypothesis.
suggestions.shipped_note: Home page leads with a hero, five product cards, editorial sections, then the method.

suggestions.title: Organise the shop by the two categories buyers actually distinguish
suggestions.why: Air fryers by shape (basket, dual basket, oven) and thermometers by job (instant-read, wireless leave-in) match how people describe what they want. 'Category' pages in the old sections were by appliance type only and ignored the thermometers entirely.
suggestions.confidence: Hypothesis.
suggestions.shipped_note: shop/categories/ has an Air fryers and a Thermometers page, both linked from the main navigation and both in the sitemap.

suggestions.title: Publish the three question-shaped guides with answerable FAQs
suggestions.why: Question-shaped pages can earn a featured answer and give a reader a reason to arrive. Each guide ends with an FAQ whose answers are either sourced or explicitly framed as advice.
suggestions.confidence: Hypothesis — no search-volume data was obtained or claimed.
suggestions.shipped_note: Three guides live; two more scheduled on the editorial calendar and published as drafts with honest notes, not filler.

suggestions.title: Give every page its own canonical URL, structured data, sitemap and feed
suggestions.why: One indexable site needs one set of URLs, one sitemap and a feed that search engines can subscribe to. Structured data is what lets a result carry a headline and a breadcrumb rather than a bare link.
suggestions.confidence: High on mechanics; result effects are not guaranteed by any markup.
suggestions.shipped_note: Per-page canonical, BreadcrumbList, Article and ItemList JSON-LD, plus FAQPage on guides. sitemap.xml, feed.xml and robots.txt are generated by the build.

suggestions.title: Replace the old register pages with one buyer-readable table of record, and keep the audit language behind it
suggestions.why: A reader wants to know which machine does what. An auditor wants to know what was observed and when. Both are legitimate, so the shop splits them: product pages for the buyer, one Table of record for the audit.
suggestions.confidence: High — the previous pages read as an audit to every reviewer who saw them.
suggestions.shipped_note: shop/table/ holds the full observation register with source links; product pages cite it rather than repeat it.

suggestions.title: Use editorial photography that is clearly not the product, and say so
suggestions.why: Amazon's IP licence restricts use of Amazon-served imagery, and misrepresenting a stock photo as the product would be a misleading claim. Food photography sets a mood; a caption under each image says what it is.
suggestions.confidence: High on the compliance reason; stylistic effect is a judgement.
suggestions.shipped_note: Three generated editorial images, each captioned as an illustration with no product shown.

suggestions.title: Write a plain-language About page that admits the AI assistance
suggestions.why: Readers forgive a lot; they do not forgive being misled about who wrote the page. The About page names the account holder, the role of AI assistance and the sourcing standard.
suggestions.confidence: High on the trust argument.

suggestions.title: Cut the navigation to one group of five labels
suggestions.why: The previous pages spread fifteen destinations across every section, which reads as an internal tool. Five labels — Shop, Categories, Guides, About, Suggestions — cover every reader need. Everything else lives in the footer.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.shipped_note: One navigation group sitewide; the full site map is one click away in the footer.

suggestions.title: Keep every dashboard surface reachable from the footer
suggestions.why: The brief asked for the dashboards to stay reachable while the front page became a publication. That means footer links, not primary navigation.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.shipped_note: Footer carries the Table of record, the Audit trail, the Site map and links to the older sections that still exist in this repository.

suggestions.title: Make the disclosure position and link markup machine-checked, not remembered
suggestions.why: A rule that depends on a person remembering it will eventually break, usually on the page that matters. Two checks now run on every build and in CI.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.shipped_note: tools/shop_check.py: disclosure before first outbound link on every page, every Amazon link carries rel sponsored + tag, every local link resolves, every page has a canonical and a title, XML parses.

suggestions.title: Retire the two older sections, or keep them as archives
suggestions.why: The repository currently publishes three overlapping sites from one host: the root storefront, crisp/ and shop/. That splits link equity and duplicates topics. The shop now covers the same ground better, so the choice is whether to redirect the old pages into the shop or freeze them with a note.
suggestions.confidence: High on the SEO cost of duplicate topics; the best remedy is your call.
options: Redirect: replace the old entry pages with a small page that links into the equivalent shop page, and drop them from the sitemaps.
Archive: leave the pages live, mark them as historical, and keep them out of the sitemap.
Do nothing: keep all three live and accept the split.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Search Console coverage report after the first crawl would show which pages are competing.
suggestions.blocked_by: Decision. The files belong to other sessions' scopes, so this session will not edit them.

suggestions.title: Decide whether to publish outbound-click counts as social proof
suggestions.why: A shop that can say '412 readers went to this listing last month' feels alive. It is also a claim about traffic, and if the number is small it works against you. This needs a decision before any collector is built.
suggestions.confidence: Hypothesis either way.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A few weeks of real numbers to see whether they flatter or embarrass the shop.

suggestions.title: Choose a reader-capture provider, or decide not to capture at all
suggestions.why: An email list is the only audience asset that survives an algorithm change. It also creates a privacy obligation, a consent banner and a data processor. Doing it badly is worse than not doing it.
suggestions.confidence: High that a list is valuable; the provider choice is a judgement.
options: No capture for now: keep the site entirely cookieless and say so on the Privacy page.
A privacy-first hosted provider with a double opt-in and a short privacy notice.
Self-hosted collector plus a newsletter tool once there is enough traffic to justify the upkeep.

suggestions.title: Submit the shop sitemap in Search Console and confirm indexing
suggestions.why: Being findable is not the same as being indexed. Nothing on this site can verify that Google has crawled it; only Search Console can show coverage, queries and errors.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A verified property and a sitemap submission under the account.
suggestions.blocked_by: Account access to Search Console for this host.

suggestions.title: Consolidate the host to one canonical set of URLs
suggestions.why: Three sections, thirty-plus pages and two sitemap sets currently share one origin. Google will pick its own canonical if the site does not state one clearly. The shop declares its own; the older pages do not point at it.
suggestions.confidence: High on the mechanism.
suggestions.evidence_needed: None for the first step: add a canonical or a redirect from the older entry pages into the shop.
suggestions.blocked_by: Scopes owned by other sessions; logged as a request rather than edited.

suggestions.title: Run the one-link test in the Associates dashboard before promoting anything
suggestions.why: Every link on this site points at a direct /dp/ URL carrying ?tag=shopnow047c-20. Nobody has yet confirmed that a click on that URL appears in the tracking report. Until one click is confirmed, the whole shop is an unverified channel.
suggestions.confidence: High.
suggestions.evidence_needed: One click, signed in, and the click appearing under shopnow047c-20 with a date.

suggestions.title: Adopt the Creators API to publish live prices lawfully
suggestions.why: The single most-wanted piece of information on a product page is the price. Program Policies 2(b) allows publishing it if it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. That turns the biggest gap on this site into a feature.
suggestions.confidence: High on the policy route; implementation depends on approval.
suggestions.evidence_needed: API credentials and a build step that refreshes prices, plus a display that is truthful about freshness.

suggestions.title: Buy, test and photograph the five appliances
suggestions.why: The gap between this site and a shop people bookmark is first-hand experience. Testing lets the pages state what a machine is like to live with, which is the one thing a listing cannot tell you and an AI cannot invent.
suggestions.confidence: High, and the FTC's guidance on endorsements requires an honest experience to endorse anyway.
suggestions.evidence_needed: One unit per product, a method, and a dated record per test.
suggestions.blocked_by: No units available to this session.

suggestions.title: Deploy a first-party, cookieless click counter
suggestions.why: The shop needs to know which product cards earn clicks before it can improve them. A counter that stores only 'page X, product Y, day Z, count' answers that without identifying anyone.
suggestions.confidence: High on feasibility, neutral on outcome.
suggestions.evidence_needed: A host that can run a small process. GitHub Pages cannot.
suggestions.note: The site already sends the event if an endpoint is configured; with none configured, nothing is transmitted.

suggestions.title: Collect a handful of real reader testimonials, with permission
suggestions.why: One sentence from a real buyer, used with permission and disclosed, does more than a page of method description. It also has to be genuine, which is why this cannot be written here.
suggestions.confidence: High, but only if the testimonials are real.
suggestions.evidence_needed: Written permission from each buyer and a record of what they actually said.

suggestions.title: Publish star ratings and review counts scraped from the listing
suggestions.why: Rejected. Program Policies 2(b) and section 6(a) restrict displaying and altering Program Content, and scraped numbers go stale silently. A stale rating is a misleading claim about a product.
suggestions.confidence: High on the compliance risk.
suggestions.note: Rejected on policy grounds, not on taste.

suggestions.title: Add countdown timers and 'today only' deal badges
suggestions.why: Rejected. Program Policies 2(b) requires removing links and references to a limited-time promotion as soon as the promotion ends. A countdown creates a permanent removal obligation and a false urgency claim when it is wrong.
suggestions.confidence: High.
